transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because things at home have gotten twisted up, and nobody seems to want to say it plainly. My husband’s sister, she’s been working this family business—always right there, always acting like she’s just helping—and I can see what she’s doing. She’s trying to get control of the money and push me out of the decisions.

People keep telling me, “Oh, don’t worry about it,” or they try to smooth it over like families do, you know, especially when there’s money involved… reminds me of how my mother used to say never mix family and business. But I know what I’ve been seeing. This has been going on more than a year now.
Aside from your sister-in-law, do you often find yourself feeling that other people—friends, coworkers, or family—are trying to deceive or take advantage of you?

Not really everybody, no… I mean, people can be funny when money’s involved, you know, family especially. My mother used to say that, and she was right about a lot of things even if she had her ways.

But the reason I came is because of my husband’s sister. She’s been in that family business, always acting like she’s just helping, but I can see she’s setting it up so she gets control of the money and I get pushed out of the decisions. And folks keep trying to smooth it over like I’m making too much of it, but this has been going on more than a year. I know what I’ve been seeing.

Thinking back to your teenage years and early twenties, before this situation with your sister-in-law, would you say you generally had a hard time trusting other people—like friends, coworkers, or romantic partners—or is this kind of deep suspicion something new for you?

I don’t know… I mean, that was a long time ago. I had friends and all that, and people had their little dramas back then, you know how girls can be in school. I didn’t finish like I maybe should’ve, but life just sort of went the way it went.

I wouldn’t say I walked around thinking everyone was out to get me, if that’s what you mean. This thing now feels different because it’s right in front of me, with the business and the money and family getting all involved. That’s not the same as just being young and figuring people out.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to hear or see?

I don’t think so… I mean, sometimes you hear a noise in the house and you wonder what it is, especially at night, but that’s just houses settling or neighbors, you know. My old house used to make all kinds of sounds when the heat came on.

But no, not like seeing things other people don’t see or hearing voices talking to me, if that’s what you mean. It’s more what’s happening right in front of everybody, with the business and how people act like they don’t notice.
Aside from this situation with your sister-in-law, how have things been going for you day-to-day—are you still able to keep up with your usual routines, work, and relationships without much trouble?

Day to day, I still do most of what I always did. I go to my quilting group, and choir practice when we have it—though last week they changed the time and nobody told me until late, but that’s a whole other thing. I’m still doing my GED lessons too, trying to keep my brain working, and I do those senior walks.

So no, it hasn’t stopped me from living my life exactly. It’s more that I don’t trust my husband’s sister now, and I’m more careful about which family gatherings I go to. Some of those get-togethers, I just don’t feel comfortable being there if she’s around acting sweet like nothing’s going on.
